# Sirach Chapter 28 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 28 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**Council Notes:**
Chapter 28 is one of Sirach's great chapters. It opens with a call to forgiveness grounded in one's own need for forgiveness (vv. 1-7) — a passage structurally parallel to the Lord's Prayer ("forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors"). The second half is dominated by the "tongue" motif, building to the famous v. 18: "Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not so many as have fallen because of the tongue." This is one of the most quoted verses in Sirach. The chapter closes with the extended metaphor of the tongue as fire and chains (vv. 19-23), then practical counsel for guarding the mouth (vv. 24-26).

The "third tongue" (γλῶσσα τρίτη) in vv. 14-15 is a rabbinic idiom for the gossip/slanderer — a "third" inserted between two people. It does not mean a literally third person, but a troublemaking intermediary.

---

**28:1** He who takes vengeance will receive vengeance from the LORD, and the LORD will keep firm account of his sins.

**28:2** Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done you, and then your sins will be forgiven when you pray.

**28:3** Does a man harbor anger against a man — and then seek healing from the LORD?

**28:4** He has no mercy on a man like himself — yet he makes petition about his own sins?

**28:5** He himself, being flesh, holds on to wrath — who then will atone for his sins?

**28:6** Remember your last things and cease from hatred; remember corruption and death and keep the commandments.

**28:7** Remember the commandments and do not be angry with your neighbor; remember the covenant of the Most High and overlook the offense.

**28:8** Keep away from strife and you will diminish your sins; for the hot-tempered person fans the flames of strife,

**28:9** and a sinful man troubles his friends and throws enmity among those who are at peace.

**28:10** According to the fuel of the fire, so it burns; and according to the stubbornness of a man, so the strife grows great; and according to his strength, so the anger grows hotter.

**28:11** A quarrel rushed into kindles a fire, and a hasty dispute sheds blood.

**28:12** If you blow on a spark it blazes up; if you spit on it, it goes out — and both come from your mouth.

**28:13** Curse the whisperer and the double-tongued, for they have destroyed many who were at peace.

**28:14** The third tongue has shaken many loose and scattered them from nation to nation; it has destroyed fortified cities and overturned the houses of great men.

**28:15** The third tongue has driven capable wives from their homes and deprived them of the fruit of their labors.

**28:16** Whoever gives heed to it will find no rest, and will not dwell in quietness.

**28:17** The blow of a whip raises a bruise, but the blow of the tongue shatters bones.

**28:18** Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not so many as have fallen because of the tongue.

**28:19** Blessed is the man who has been sheltered from it, who has not passed through its fury, who has not dragged its yoke or been bound in its chains.

**28:20** For its yoke is a yoke of iron and its chains are chains of bronze.

**28:21** The death it brings is an evil death, and Hades is preferable to it.

**28:22** It will have no power over the devout; they will not be burned in its flame.

**28:23** Those who forsake the LORD will fall into it; in them it will burn and not be quenched. It will be sent against them like a lion and ravage them like a leopard.

**28:24** Fence your fields with thorns; bind your silver and gold securely.

**28:25** And make for your mouth a door and a bolt; and for your words a balance and a scale.

**28:26** Take care lest you stumble through it and fall before one who lies in wait for you.
